text:
Charlie Lindgren's starts have come in spurts this season, and few of them have gone his way. Eight starts, a 3-5-0 record, an .848 save percentage, and 6.5 goals allowed beyond what an average goalie would give up on the same shots (28 on 21.5 expected), 8th percentile among goalies with a real sample. Last season ended at -5.9 in 21 games by our measure, so this isn't brand new. In 2023-24, when he played 50 games, Evolving-Hockey had him well above expected on their scale.

The damage is mostly in the middle: .783 on medium-danger shots against a league .861. Those are the shots a goalie in his role has to eat to earn more nights. One thing he does well is tidy: 8.3% of his saves lead to another shot within three seconds, against a league 10.7%. The recent nights haven't helped. He allowed six to New Jersey on Nov. 14 and six more in Boston on Saturday, which CBS Sports summed up in one word: "Leaky." He went undrafted out of St. Cloud State and earned his way here, so he knows how to climb out of a hole.
headline: Charlie Lindgren's spot starts keep going sideways
